title: Medical Oxygen Access And Facility Readiness Gaps In LMICs
summary: Build a verified workflow for separating medical oxygen need, facility oxygen readiness, supply reliability, and financing gaps in low- and middle-income countries.
why_it_matters: Health ministries, global health funders, and oxygen market-shaping partners decide whether to finance concentrators, liquid oxygen, cylinders, pulse oximetry, maintenance, or tariff reform. Verified evidence can change those allocations only if it separates oxygen need from equipment presence, uptime, clinical use, and supply-chain reliability.

success_metrics.target: Accepted artifacts distinguish clinical oxygen need, facility oxygen availability, pulse oximetry availability, and supply reliability.
success_metrics.validation_method: Reviewer checks datasets.md, evidence.json, and validation.md for separate numerator, denominator, grain, and limitation notes.

success_metrics.target: Every operational artifact names the ministry, funder, or procurement decision it could inform and the observation that would overturn it.
success_metrics.validation_method: Review outputs.md and playbooks.md for named user, decision timing, non-use cases, and kill condition.

success_metrics.target: No claim treats oxygen equipment presence as proof of oxygen access without uptime, consumables, power, trained staff, and clinical-use context.
success_metrics.validation_method: Domain reviewer checks evidence limitations and red-team review before any quantitative comparison advances.

review_policy.merge_gate: Schema validation, domain review, red-team review for allocation-sensitive outputs, and replication for quantitative readiness or shortage classifications.
